step_ma.reference: alexgrover, T-Step LSMA and T-Channels (TradingView); Goblin Town ladder average (strategy code)
step_ma.matches_strategy_copies: yes: f66235c41bc1 (tstep_lsma, full script ported), 5dd1a82ae1e5 (deadband_double_sma), f4e22c0b71d1 (step_line with the script's dev band; the script also forces a = src for bar_index < 9, warm-up only)

strategy_issues.issue: The efficiency ratio of the band mixes series: er = abs(change(src, length)) / sum(abs(change(src10)), length) uses close (src) in the numerator and the RSI-like rr (src10) in the denominator, so er is not confined to 0..1 and the dev band weights are meaningless.

The deviation term d = cum(abs(src[length_] - ma))/bar_index*gamma reads the script's input `src` (= open) while the line itself is built on src_ (= close); pass open as deviation_source to reproduce, close for the consistent version. With gamma = 4 the band is so wide that the line hardly ever moves.

step_ma.notes: Three related constructions under one name: generic deadband step (step_line), alexgrover's cumulative-deviation step (tchannels, tstep_lsma) and the Goblin Town double-SMA deadband (deadband_double_sma). T-Step LSMA uses Pine's stdev epsilon (deviations <= 1e-10 are 0), so a flat step line gives an na fit as in Pine instead of rounding noise.
